title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) System Malfunction
shortDescription: The electric power steering (EPS) system has set P1700: electric power steering (eps) system malfunction. Steering effort may increase suddenly.
fullDescription: Modern vehicles use electric power steering instead of a hydraulic pump. The EPS module reads driver torque input, vehicle speed and steering angle, then commands an assist motor on the column or rack. P1700 indicates the EPS controller detected a fault matching 'Electric Power Steering (EPS) System Malfunction'. Depending on severity the system may continue at reduced assist, or fully disable assist and illuminate the steering warning on the cluster. Manual steering effort then becomes very high, especially at parking-lot speeds.
safetyImpact: Sudden loss of power steering assist greatly increases steering effort and can surprise the driver, especially during low-speed maneuvers. Repair without delay.

causes.cause: Faulty EPS torque or angle sensor inside the steering column
EPS assist motor electrical or mechanical failure
Low battery voltage or weak alternator triggering EPS protection
CAN bus communication fault between EPS, ABS and PCM modules
Damaged wiring harness or connector to the EPS module
EPS module internal failure or corrupt software calibration

symptoms: Steering wheel becomes heavy or stiff
EPS or steering warning light illuminated on the dash
Intermittent loss of power assist
Steering pulls or has dead spot on-center
Steering angle calibration lost after battery disconnect

fixSteps.title: Check Battery and Charging System
fixSteps.instruction: Verify battery voltage at rest (12.6V+) and with engine running (13.8-14.7V). Weak batteries are a top cause of EPS faults because the assist motor draws high current.

fixSteps.title: Scan EPS Module
fixSteps.instruction: Use a capable scan tool that can access the EPS / steering control module — generic OBD-II readers usually cannot. Read DTCs and freeze frame, note any companion ABS or stability control codes.
tools: bidirectional scan tool with EPS coverage

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring and Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the high-current EPS power feed and ground for corrosion or loose terminals. Wiggle-test the column harness while watching live data; flickers point to broken wiring.

fixSteps.title: Perform Steering Angle Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: After any battery disconnect, alignment, or column work the steering angle sensor must be re-zeroed. Many vehicles require a scan tool to perform this calibration.

fixSteps.title: Replace EPS Components
fixSteps.instruction: If the torque sensor, motor, or module is confirmed bad, replacement usually means swapping the whole steering column or rack assembly. After installation, perform calibration and a road test.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with the EPS warning on?
faq.a: Steering is mechanical even with EPS off, so the car remains drivable, but effort is much higher — particularly when parking. Drive carefully to a shop or home.

faq.q: Can a low battery really cause an EPS code?
faq.a: Yes. The EPS motor draws 60-90 amps under heavy assist. If the battery is weak, system voltage sags below threshold and the module disables assist as a protection measure.

faq.q: Does the EPS need calibration after every battery change?
faq.a: Many vehicles require a steering-angle reset after the battery is disconnected. Some self-learn after a few cycles of driving, others need a scan tool. Check the service manual for your specific model.

fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the high-current EPS power feed and ground for corrosion or loose terminals. Wiggle-test the column harness while watching live data; flickers point to broken wiring.

fixSteps.title: Perform Steering Angle Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: After any battery disconnect, alignment, or column work the steering angle sensor must be re-zeroed. Many vehicles require a scan tool to perform this calibration.

fixSteps.title: Replace EPS Components
fixSteps.instruction: If the torque sensor, motor, or module is confirmed bad, replacement usually means swapping the whole steering column or rack assembly. After installation, perform calibration and a road test.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with the EPS warning on?
faq.a: Steering is mechanical even with EPS off, so the car remains drivable, but effort is much higher — particularly when parking. Drive carefully to a shop or home.

faq.q: Can a low battery really cause an EPS code?
faq.a: Yes. The EPS motor draws 60-90 amps under heavy assist. If the battery is weak, system voltage sags below threshold and the module disables assist as a protection measure.

faq.q: Does the EPS need calibration after every battery change?
faq.a: Many vehicles require a steering-angle reset after the battery is disconnected. Some self-learn after a few cycles of driving, others need a scan tool. Check the service manual for your specific model.
